attempts.summary: On node1, built a local flat apt repository at /srv/localrepo (cowsay + sl .debs, indexed with apt-ftparchive), served it via python3 http.server bound to $NODE_IP:8080, added it as a trusted apt source, then made the real Ubuntu archive/security mirrors unreachable via /etc/hosts redirection to 127.0.0.1 (nothing listening there → connection refused). With remotes confirmed unreachable, ran apt-get update (remote repos errored, local repo succeeded) and apt-get install -y cowsay, which installed and ran successfully from local storage only. Restored /etc/hosts and removed the temporary sources.list.d entry afterward as cleanup. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured baseline boot_id (8d1d94e2...) and proof of health (cowsay installed, local repo files present, HTTP listener up), triggered a scheduled reboot via systemd-run so the ack returned before disconnect, polled through the outage, confirmed a new boot_id (b469d415...) proving a real restart, and verified post-restart that the cowsay package and repo files persisted (the ad-hoc python http.server, being a foreground process and not a systemd service, did not persist across reboot, as expected/correct).
